children: National Stock Exchange of India (NSEI.NS) is likely to price its initial public offering at 1,700 to 1,785 rupees per share, a source aware of the matter said on Tuesday.
At the upper end of the price band, NSE would be valued at 4.4 trillion rupees ($46.41 billion), making it one of India's biggest companies by market capitalisation.

The long-awaited IPO could rank among India's biggest-ever, alongside billionaire Mukesh ​Ambani's Jio Platforms. NSE dominates India's equity derivatives market and is the world's most-active derivatives exchange by contracts traded.
The source did not want to be identified as they are not authorized to speak to the media.
NSE did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
Reuters had reported last week that the exchange is targeting a listing in the week starting September 21.
Bloomberg News had reported the price band earlier on Tuesday.
NSE may reduce the stake being offered to about 5.5% of total equity capital from the originally planned 6%, Bloomberg News reported, citing sources. Reuters could not immediately verify this.
